package_info.package_name: imageless malicious Docker Hub repository (Downloader, eBook Phishing, Website SEO campaigns)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (repository-based, not versioned like code packages)
package_info.why_malicious: These repositories are intentionally created without container images but with malicious metadata (such as README files or descriptions) containing links to phishing sites, malware downloads, or scam offers. The campaigns exploit Docker Hub's trust and searchability to lure users into credential theft or malware infection, often using automation to create large numbers of repositories at scale.

execution_context.trigger: repository discovery or search-time (when user browses or views repository page)
execution_context.file_location: repository metadata (README.md, description field, repository homepage link)
required_permissions: network (user browser required to access external links)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
README.md or description field contains external URLs, such as:

[Download eBook](http://malicious-phishing-site.com/ebook-download)

Or:

Visit our website for a free giveaway: http://malicious-seo-campaign.com

No container image is present in the repository.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At repository discovery or search-time, the repository metadata displays external links in the README or description, which, when clicked by the user, direct the user's browser to a phishing or malware site, resulting in potential credential theft or malware infection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Legitimate Docker Hub repositories are expected to provide container images and technical documentation relevant to the software. Repositories with no images but with metadata containing external links to unrelated or suspicious domains are highly indicative of malicious intent, especially when created in large, automated batches.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal repositories provide container images and documentation about the software; these repositories lack images and instead use metadata solely to promote external, unrelated, or malicious links.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate repositories may include links to official documentation or project websites, but these are typically supplementary to the container image and are not the sole content. They also do not link to unrelated, suspicious, or known malicious domains.
key_indicators: Absence of any container image or image layers in the repository
README.md or description field contains external URLs to non-Docker, unrelated, or suspicious domains
Repository metadata includes keywords such as 'download', 'giveaway', 'free', or references to unrelated offers
Large-scale, automated creation of similar repositories by the same user or small group of users
External links in metadata point to domains associated with phishing, malware, or SEO spam campaigns

attack_chain.action: Automated creation of large numbers of imageless repositories on Docker Hub, each with malicious metadata (README or description containing links to phishing or malware sites).
attack_chain.leads_to: User discovers the repository via Docker Hub search or browsing.

attack_chain.action: User views the repository page and is presented with metadata containing enticing external links (e.g., 'Download eBook', 'Free Giveaway').
attack_chain.leads_to: User clicks the external link in the metadata and is redirected to a phishing or malware site.

attack_chain.action: Phishing or malware site attempts to steal user credentials or deliver malware to the user's system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Credential theft, malware infection, or user engagement with scam offers.

behavioral_signatures: Repositories with no container images but with non-empty README.md or description fields containing external URLs
Automated, large-scale creation of repositories by a single user or small set of accounts
Repository metadata containing keywords such as 'download', 'giveaway', 'free', or references to unrelated offers
External links in metadata pointing to domains not associated with Docker, official documentation, or the project
file_indicators: Repositories with empty or missing image layers
README.md or description fields containing URLs to non-Docker, unrelated, or suspicious domains
Metadata fields populated with repetitive or templated content across many repositories
network_indicators: External links in repository metadata pointing to known phishing, malware, or SEO spam domains
Unusual outbound HTTP/HTTPS traffic from Docker Hub users to suspicious external sites immediately after repository browsing
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor Docker Hub for repositories lacking container images but with non-empty README.md or description fields containing external URLs, especially those created in large batches or by accounts with high-volume automated activity. Flag repositories whose metadata links to known phishing, malware, or SEO spam domains. Alert on user activity that follows such links from repository pages to external sites. Correlate repository creation patterns, metadata content, and user click-through behavior to identify and disrupt malicious campaigns.
